findings.text: Distance presence query reports whether a given interconnect distance value appears in the scheduler NUMA level table, with an immediate positive answer for the self distance and otherwise a bounded scan under read-side protection. It returns a boolean and leaves caller state unchanged.

Task NUMA teardown detaches a task from its group and manages its fault storage. When a group is present it subtracts the task contribution and drops membership under protection before releasing the group reference and clearing the link. Final teardown frees the buffer, non-final teardown zeroes totals and per-node counters.

Hint fault accounting ingests fault location, volume and flags for the current task, lazily provisions per-node fault storage, classifies accesses as private or shared, optionally triggers group formation, reclassifies qualifying shared faults as local, periodically invokes placement and preferred-node retry, and accumulates migration and locality statistics.

Deferred NUMA work performs periodic address-space scanning eligibility checks and preparation. It ignores exiting tasks and single-node cpuset confinement, enforces a maximum scan frequency with an atomic next-scan update, initializes scan timing on first use, derives page and virtual budgets, acquires the address-space lock opportunistically, and sets up pid-aware VMA iteration with a forced rescan path.

Preferred-node handling favors settling grouped workloads on active nodes and avoids pinning second-choice placements. Migration retry is scheduled at a fraction of the current scan period bounded above, skipped when statistics are absent or the task already resides on its preferred node, and otherwise reattempts placement. A placement attempt with no superior destination reports a retryable failure, while successful selection either moves a lone task or exchanges a pair and clears the destination migration flag.

Per-node fault windows decay historic values by half while folding newly buffered memory and CPU observations, preserving totals. CPU contributions are normalized by recent execution share so low-runtime tasks weigh less, group aggregates mirror task deltas when grouped, and an optional cache footprint heuristic absorbs the same deltas with clamping against negative wrap.

Scan timing adapts to idleness, failure and locality. Idle or uninteresting activity and recorded migration failures lengthen the interval geometrically and defer the next address-space scan. Otherwise locality and privateness ratios scaled to a fixed slot count lengthen the interval when accesses are mostly local or mostly shared and shorten it when private remote faults dominate, always clamped between task-specific bounds with locality counters reset.

Grouping and preference combine fault majority with topology awareness. Active-node count reflects nodes whose fault volume scaled by a fraction exceeds the peak. New groups copy the originator fault image and start singleton; joining prefers the larger membership with address tie-break and requires same address space or a shared marker, transferring fault images and counts atomically. Preferred-node choice is identity on direct interconnects, maximum weight on mesh, and recursive highest-fault cluster narrowing on backplane systems.

Group statistics mutation requires the group lock with interrupts masked; cross-group transfer acquires both group locks in address order with nesting. Distance table and group pointer reads use read-side critical sections. Scan sequence uses single-access load and store without exclusivity as a sampling heuristic. Fault buffer allocation and group creation occur outside locks; reference acquisition must succeed before leaving the read-side section when joining.

The group aggregates shared NUMA state: a fault array sized by hint-stat kinds times node count, total faults, task count, group identifier, active-node count, peak CPU fault value, an interrupt-safe lock, a reference count with delayed reclamation, and a callback head. Identity and counts support join preference and active-set tests.

Task NUMA state comprises a fault buffer indexed by region node and privacy, total faults, a three-slot locality summary, preferred node, scan period and bounds, scan sequence, migration retry instant, runtime snapshots for averaging, migrated-page count, deferred work item and group pointer. Address-space state carries next-scan time, scan sequence and offset; VMA state carries scan start and previous sequences plus active pid bitmaps.

Balancing cycles through fault observation, sequence-guarded placement, preferred-node migration and deferred virtual scanning. Faults fill buffers until a retry deadline triggers placement and migration; placement folds buffers, selects a fault-majority node mapped to a CPU-bearing node and refreshes timing; deferred work advances the scan offset and wraps with a sequence bump; VMA eligibility moves from unconditional early scans to pid-filtered, in-progress-tolerant and starvation-forced scans.

Races include concurrent scan-sequence updates treated as sampling noise, racy footprint accumulation with clamped subtraction on exit, backward-moving placement timestamps guarded to zero, allocation failure paths that silently skip accounting or grouping, mismatched fault identity that aborts joining, and reference drops that must pair every successful acquisition and every detached membership to avoid leaks or premature reclamation.
Scan adaptation uses ten period slots with a threshold of seven distinguishing slower from faster scanning.
The VMA pid activity reset interval equals four times the configured balancing scan delay.
